guitar.guitaristsText: Jim Martin / Dean Menta / Jon Hudson
guitar.notes: Band had several guitarists across its history; Jim Martin used various rock guitars but nothing singularly iconic.

tone.target: mid-gain alt-metal crunch with tight chorus sheen
tone.profile: mid-gain alt-metal crunch with tight chorus sheen
tone.summary: A tight, mid-gain signal chain using an OD boost for bite, followed by a classic Marshall amp model and Chorus effect to achieve the required crunchy, punchy tone.
corrections: keep it crunchy, not modern high gain

rig.name: Faith No More - Epic - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up pick noise and hum.
Provide aggressive pick attack and mid-range bite for tight palm-muting.
blocks.gap: The Blues OD is chosen over Green OD/OD 9 to provide a slightly warmer, more rounded crunch suitable for alt-metal without sounding too thin.

blocks.purpose: Add necessary mid-range grit and sustain to complement the OD boost without becoming overly fuzzy.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style is used sparingly (low drive) to add crunch texture rather than heavy fuzz, fulfilling the 'crunchy, not modern high gain' requirement.

blocks.purpose: Bypass (No wah needed for this tone).
blocks.gap: The target tone does not require a specific filter sweep.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic Marshall-style crunch and solid low end.
blocks.gap: None. This model is ideal for alt-metal/classic rock punchiness.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the required Marshall-style 4x12 cabinet sound.
Add the required 'chorus sheen' and width to the overall tone.
Minimal delay for subtle depth (kept mostly off to avoid big tails).
blocks.gap: The effect is kept minimal and largely bypassed, as the verdict advises against 'big delay tails'.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle space and glue to the mix without sounding overly ambient.
blocks.gap: A small amount of Room reverb is used for depth, balancing the aggressive crunch.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for better cabinet realism and definition.

proposals.reason: Improve the perceived depth and punch of the Marshall style cab.
